memory.title: Persistent memory
memory.intro: If enabled, the assistant automatically learns durable facts about you (preferences, role, technologies) and remembers them across chats. Each fact requires your confirmation before being stored.
memory.autoMemoryHint: Automatic fact extraction at the end of the conversation.
memory.thresholdHint: Number of new messages before an automatic extraction. Empty = use the global default.
memory.sharedMemoryHint: Use the notes your teams and the organisation share, in every chat. Independent of the automatic memory: you can use one, the other or both.
memory.duplicatesWarning: The episodic memory (Recordare) also learns your tastes and habits: with both on, the same thing may be stored twice. You can copy Recordare's notes here from Diary → Who you are instead.
memory.noFacts: No facts yet. They'll be proposed during conversations.
memory.mergeProposal: Merge: will replace the original notes
memory.graphHint: Hover a node to read the note. Links come from the evolution job.
memory.episodicIntro: If enabled, your chats are also sent to Recordare, the installation's episodic memory service: it remembers what happened and when (events, plans, changes) and the assistant can search it. Independent of the persistent memory above.
memory.episodicHint: From the moment you turn it on, Recordare stores your chats and extracts memories from them; turn it off to stop sending them.
memory.episodicModePersonalHint: Personal: what you say becomes the agent's own memory, in the first person — an indirect digital twin of you. Other users who speak in your shared chats are recognised by name inside this memory.
memory.episodicModeEntityHint: Entity: a shared agent (e.g. the home voice assistant, a robot): whoever speaks without being identified is "someone"; identified people are remembered by name.
memory.episodicModeHint: It can only be changed while the memory is empty.
memory.episodicEntityNotice: Entity memory: everyone using this account reads and writes all its memories. Do not use it for private matters.
memory.genderHint: How the memory speaks of itself in gendered languages (e.g. Italian "sono andato" / "sono andata"). Default: masculine.
memory.episodicAtlasHint: The live view of the memory (admins only: it shows every person's activity).

recordare.title: Recordare — connection
recordare.intro: Recordare is the episodic memory service: it remembers every user's conversations, facts and plans. Here you say where it is and which key Arkimede presents. Changes apply at once, no restart.
recordare.urlHelp: The service's base address as Arkimede's backend reaches it (e.g. http://recordare:8080 on the same Docker network, or https://memory.example.com). Empty = the server's RECORDARE_URL.
recordare.apiKeyHelp: The rk_… key of the «Arkimede» client, created in Recordare's console (Clients → New client). Used for every call. Leave empty to keep the stored one.
recordare.sourceLegend: Each value comes from these settings or, when empty here, from the server's environment (RECORDARE_URL, RECORDARE_API_KEY, RECORDARE_WEBHOOK_SECRET). Keys are stored encrypted.

errors.recordare.invalidUrl: Invalid address: http:// or https:// needed
errors.recordare.invalidWebhookSecret: The secret must start with whsec_

recordare.initiativesIntro: Initiatives are what the memory decides to say on its own: a reminder you asked for, a question about how something went, something left unfinished. Recordare decides who, when and on which channel and pushes it to Arkimede with a signed webhook; Arkimede writes it in the user's «Recordare» chat with a notification. Without the webhook initiatives still arrive, but only when the user opens Arkimede or at the periodic check (every 15 minutes).
recordare.step2: In Recordare's console: Clients → Arkimede → Webhooks → Add; paste the address and choose the initiative.deliver event. In the client's channels set «chat» with reach «always».
recordare.step3: Recordare shows the whsec_… secret once: paste it here and save.
recordare.webhookUrlHelp: Where Recordare delivers initiatives. It is this page's address: if Recordare runs on the same server in Docker you may need the backend's internal address (e.g. http://backend:3000/api/recordare/webhook). Recordare must be able to reach it.
recordare.eventsHelp: initiative.deliver is enough (deliver now). The other events are information only and Arkimede ignores them.
recordare.webhookSecretHelp: The whsec_… secret Recordare gives at registration: Arkimede checks every delivery's signature with it and refuses the others. Without a secret the webhook is off (answers 404).
recordare.lastWebhookHelp: The last delivery with a valid signature since the backend started: if it stays empty after an initiative, check the address and the secret.

usage.servingLiveHint: Live dispatcher snapshot (refreshed every 5s). "—" = config without a concurrency cap (pass-through).

isolation.title: Network isolation level
isolation.subtitle: How skill and sandbox executions are isolated in this deployment. Detected live by probing the job broker and the egress proxy.
isolation.level1Desc: No job broker: skills run in-process inside the executor service. Simplest setup, weakest isolation.
isolation.level2Desc: Job broker active: every skill/sandbox run happens in an ephemeral hardened container attached to an internal network with no route to the internet (grants add reach per skill).
isolation.level3Desc: Isolated + egress proxy: runs with internet access go through an allowlisting proxy (only approved domains, e.g. pypi/npm), instead of reaching the open network.
isolation.changeIntro: The level is part of the Docker Compose topology: restart the stack from the source checkout with the overlays you want (each -f adds one level):
isolation.changeHub: Pull-based installs (arkimede-deploy): re-run ./install-hub.sh and pick the new level — data and configuration are preserved.
isolation.runtimeNote: Note: the level itself requires a stack restart, but what each run can reach (none / internal / internet / open, plus per-skill network grants) is already configured at runtime from this page and per skill.

sandbox.netInternetUnavailable: Requires the egress proxy (isolation level 3 · Maximum) — not deployed in this stack.
sandbox.netInternetNotAllowed: The egress network is not usable: it must be declared (JOB_EGRESS_NETWORK) and included in the broker's BROKER_ALLOWED_NETWORKS.
sandbox.execTrustedUnavailable: Requires the broker opt-in BROKER_ALLOW_PRIVILEGED_SANDBOX=1 — not enabled in this stack.
sandbox.execTrustedSavedUnavailable: The saved profile is 'trusted' but the broker opt-in (BROKER_ALLOW_PRIVILEGED_SANDBOX) is not enabled: runs silently fall back to the hardened profile.
sandbox.netInternetSavedUnavailable: The saved policy is 'internet' but the egress proxy is not deployed: runs needing the network will fail (fail-closed). Pick another policy or deploy level 3.
sandbox.adminSubtitle: Enable the tool that runs arbitrary code/shell in an isolated container. Powerful capability: keep it restricted to trusted projects/teams.
sandbox.enableHint: Global master switch. When off, the tool is available to no one.
sandbox.netNoneDesc: Maximum isolation: code cannot reach any network.
sandbox.netInternalDesc: Only the platform's internal API (backend), no internet access.
sandbox.netInternetDesc: Backend + only allowlisted domains via the egress proxy (descriptive skills must declare their domains).
sandbox.netOpenDesc: Backend + unrestricted network access, no allowlist (needed for ad-hoc curl/HTTP).
sandbox.openWarning: Open internet on arbitrary code: exfiltration risk. Also requires the docker network in BROKER_ALLOWED_NETWORKS.
sandbox.execHardenedDesc: Read-only root filesystem, non-root user, all capabilities dropped. Maximum isolation.
sandbox.execTrustedDesc: The code runs as root on a writable filesystem, so it can install system libraries at runtime (apt-get). Changes are lost when the container exits.
sandbox.execTrustedWarning: Weaker isolation: only for trusted teams/projects. Also requires BROKER_ALLOW_PRIVILEGED_SANDBOX=1 on the broker; otherwise it falls back to hardened.
sandbox.allowlistHint: Admins are always authorized. A user passes if they belong to an authorized team or the chat is in an authorized project.
sandbox.runtimeInProcessDesc: Code runs as a local process with full access to the host filesystem. A deliberate development choice: do not use it with untrusted users.
sandbox.runtimeBroker: Isolated execution via broker (container per job)

dsSecurity.title: DataSource security (anti-SSRF)
dsSecurity.subtitle: Restricts which hosts DataSources/DB tools may connect to. Prevents using a DataSource to reach internal services or the cloud metadata endpoint.
dsSecurity.metadataNote: The cloud metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254 / IPv6 link-local) is always blocked, regardless of these settings.
dsSecurity.allowPrivateHint: Needed for self-hosted DBs on LAN or localhost. Turn off to allow only public hosts (plus the allowlist) for untrusted multi-tenant deployments.
dsSecurity.allowlistHint: Hosts, IPs or CIDRs allowed even when private hosts are disabled. One per line (or comma-separated).

toolLoading.adminSubtitle: Controls how many tools and with what level of detail they are injected into the agent's prompt. Reduces context tokens when using many tools.
toolLoading.userSubtitle: Customize how tools are loaded into your context. Overrides the global default for your account only.
toolLoading.strategyAlwaysDesc: Inject all tools on every request. Ideal if you have few tools (< 10).
toolLoading.strategyTopKDesc: Semantically select the K most relevant tools for the user's message. Optimal with many tools.
toolLoading.strategyAutoDesc: If tools are ≤ threshold use "Always all", otherwise switch to RAG.
toolLoading.formatFullDesc: Complete JSON schema with all descriptions. Maximum compatibility.
toolLoading.formatCompressedDesc: Only the first sentence of the description; parameter schema unchanged. ~50-70% fewer tokens per tool.
toolLoading.formatDeferredDesc: Tool with minimal description; full list injected in prompt. SKILL.md loaded on-demand via get_tool_instructions. ~80-90% fewer tokens per tool.
toolLoading.conversationMemoryHint: Limits how much conversation history is sent to the model on each request. Low values save tokens; high values keep more context. Global default, overridable per user.
toolLoading.conversationMemoryHintUser: Limits how much history is sent to the model. Low values save tokens; high values keep longer context. The global default is configured by the admin (typically 6,000 tok).
toolLoading.conversationMemoryUnitUser: max history tokens (500–32 000; empty = global default)
toolLoading.compactInsteadHint: Beyond the threshold, older turns are summarized by the summarizer model and the summary stays in context — no memory lost. If off, old turns are simply truncated.
toolLoading.compactionThresholdHint: Compaction triggers when history exceeds this % of {{budget}} tokens. Lower = more frequent and aggressive compression. The model generating summaries is set with the ✨ button in the "LLM Provider" panel.
toolLoading.persistentMemoryHint: Global default extraction threshold: every how many new messages the agent tries to extract durable facts about the user. Each user can enable memory and override this threshold from their profile.
toolLoading.globalDefaultDesc: Use the configuration set by the admin.
toolLoading.globalFormatDesc: Use the format set by the admin.

llm.formReasoningHint: hidden thinking before every answer and tool call. Off or low = much faster replies (voice).

transcription.title: Voice transcription (Whisper)
transcription.subtitle: Enable the microphone button in chat. Audio is transcribed to text by an OpenAI-compatible Whisper endpoint (cloud or self-hosted) and is never saved to disk.
transcription.enableDesc: Show the microphone button in the message composer for all users.
transcription.providerInternalDesc: Whisper service bundled with the app — ready to use
transcription.providerGroqDesc: Groq cloud — very fast and cheap
transcription.internalInfoDesc: Uses the transcription service bundled with the app (Whisper or NVIDIA Parakeet). The URL is detected from the deployment: nothing to configure. Pick the model below or keep the service's own; press "Test" to verify (and download) the active model.
transcription.apiKeyKeepPlaceholder: Leave empty to keep the current key
transcription.connectionFailed: Connection to the transcription endpoint failed
transcription.internalModelHint: The service keeps one model loaded at a time and downloads a new one on first use (Test). Whisper, indicative RAM on CPU (int8): tiny 0.3 GB · base 0.5 GB · small 1 GB · medium 2.5 GB · large-v3 4 GB · large-v3-turbo 2.5 GB (near large-v3 quality, much faster). parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 (NVIDIA Parakeet, ~1 GB, ~490 MB download): much faster than Whisper on short phrases, 25 European languages detected by itself (the configured language is ignored).
transcription.internalMissingDesc: This deployment does not include the internal transcription service (e.g. installed without voice services): the microphone stays hidden until you pick an external provider or install the service.
transcription.vocabularyDesc: Suggests the expected words to the model, so proper names and places are transcribed right.
transcription.vocabularyWordsPlaceholder: One per line or comma-separated: places, rooms, devices…
transcription.vocabularyHint: The names of the people the user's memory knows are added by themselves (when the episodic memory is on). About 500 characters reach the model: your words come first.
transcription.fallbackDesc: When the cloud provider does not answer (down, rate-limited, slow) the phrase is transcribed by a model of the bundled service.
transcription.fallbackNoLocal: No local model installed: download one by choosing it with the Internal provider and pressing Test, then come back here.
transcription.fallbackInternalMissing: The bundled transcription service is not installed: no fallback is available.
transcription.fallbackNotDownloaded: The chosen model is no longer downloaded in the bundled service: the fallback is paused.
transcription.fallbackHint: Only models already downloaded can be chosen. It is loaded on save, so it answers without waiting.

tts.title: Speech synthesis (Piper)
tts.subtitle: Lets the assistant read replies aloud (speaker button on messages) and powers the OpenAI-compatible /audio/speech route. Audio is generated on the fly and is never saved to disk.
tts.enableDesc: Shows the read-aloud button on messages and enables the /audio/speech route and the Wyoming server voice.
tts.providerInternalDesc: Piper service bundled with the app — ready to use
tts.providerCompatDesc: Self-hosted TTS with an OpenAI-compatible API
tts.internalInfoDesc: Uses the Piper service bundled with the app. The URL is detected from the deployment — nothing to configure. Missing voices are downloaded automatically on first request. Press "Test" for a verification micro-synthesis.
tts.voiceHint: Piper voice id (e.g. it_IT-paola-medium, catalog at HuggingFace rhasspy/piper-voices) or a cloud provider voice.
tts.apiKeyKeepPlaceholder: Leave empty to keep the current key
tts.connectionFailed: Connection to the speech synthesis endpoint failed
tts.internalMissingDesc: This deployment does not include the internal speech synthesis service (e.g. installed without voice services): read-aloud stays hidden until you pick an external provider or install the service.

wyoming.title: Wyoming voice server (Home Assistant)
wyoming.subtitle: Exposes the transcription and speech synthesis providers configured above over the Wyoming protocol, so Home Assistant (and any compatible hub) uses them as native STT/TTS — Voice PE satellites included. Works with any provider: internal Whisper/Piper or cloud services.
wyoming.enableHint: The protocol has no authentication: enable it on trusted networks only and restrict clients with the list below.
wyoming.allowlistLabel: Allowed clients (IPs or IPv4 CIDRs, comma-separated)
wyoming.allowlistHint: Empty = any client. Example: 192.168.1.0/24 for the whole LAN, or the Home Assistant server's IP.
wyoming.howToDesc: Settings → Devices & services → Add integration → "Wyoming Protocol" → enter this server's host and port. Then pick the new STT/TTS in your Assist pipeline and, if you set a user below, the conversation agent too.
wyoming.portHint: The port is deployment-level (WYOMING_PORT in the .env, default 10300) and must match the container's published port.
wyoming.startFailed: Configuration saved but the server did not start
wyoming.handleHint: If you pick a user, the hub also sees Arkimede as a conversation agent (in the same Wyoming integration): the whole voice pipeline runs here, with no extra components on the hub. Requests run as that user (their tools, MCP servers, memory, costs).
wyoming.persistHint: Each conversation with the voice assistant is saved as a chat of the conversation user (one chat per Home Assistant conversation).

vectordb.title: Vector Database
vectordb.subtitle: Configure the vector database and the embedding model used to index documents.
vectordb.connStringHint: Must point to a PostgreSQL with the
vectordb.collectionsSubtitle: Organise documents into separate collections. Only one can be the default.
vectordb.collectionsEmpty: No collections — create one to get started.
vectordb.collectionCreateSearchTool: Also create the semantic search tool
vectordb.collectionCreateSearchToolHint: Shared (org) tool to search the documents of this collection. It can be edited or deleted from the Tools page.
vectordb.activeCollectionSubtitle: New documents are indexed in this collection. Semantic search happens here by default.
vectordb.activeCollectionWarningBody: Changing the active collection does not move already-indexed documents. You will need to re-index all files for them to be available in the new collection.
vectordb.embeddingSubtitle: Model used to generate vectors during indexing and semantic search. Changing this configuration invalidates existing vectors if the dimension changes.
vectordb.embeddingQueryPrefixHint: Prepended to the search question only, never to the indexed documents. Empty = no prefix.
vectordb.embeddingQueryPrefixHintInternal: Empty = the search prompt declared by the model itself is used (already correct for the model in use). Fill this in only to force a different one: it then takes precedence. Prepended to the question only, never to the indexed documents.
vectordb.providerQdrantDesc: Open-source vector DB — local or Qdrant Cloud
vectordb.providerChromaDesc: Open-source vector DB — local or Chroma Cloud
vectordb.providerAstraDbDesc: Managed vector DB on DataStax Astra
vectordb.embeddingProviderInternalDesc: Service bundled with the app — ready to use
vectordb.embeddingProviderOpenAiDesc: Cloud embeddings — requires an API key
vectordb.embeddingProviderVoyageDesc: Cloud embeddings — requires an API key
vectordb.embeddingInternalInfoDesc: Uses the embedding microservice bundled with the app. URL, model and dimensions are detected automatically — nothing to configure.

voice.subtitle: Voice transcription (Whisper), speech synthesis (Piper) and the Wyoming server for voice hubs such as Home Assistant.
voice.internalNotInstalledHint: The internal service is not present in this deployment

mcpSecurity.subtitle: Restricts which hosts http/sse MCP servers may connect to. Prevents using an MCP server to reach internal services or the cloud metadata endpoint.
mcpSecurity.metadataNote: The cloud metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254 / IPv6 link-local) is always blocked, regardless of these settings.
mcpSecurity.allowPrivateHint: Needed for self-hosted MCP servers on LAN or localhost. Disable to allow only public hosts (plus the allowlist) in untrusted multi-tenant deployments.
mcpSecurity.allowlistHint: Hosts, IPs or CIDRs allowed even when private hosts are disabled. One per line (or comma-separated).

apiKeys.title: API keys
apiKeys.subtitle: Long-lived credentials for external integrations (voice satellites, scripts, third-party clients). They work as Bearer tokens on the whole API with your identity.
apiKeys.createdOnce: Key created. Copy it now: it will never be shown again.
apiKeys.revokeConfirm: Revoke the key "{{name}}"? Integrations using it will stop working.
apiKeys.persistHint: Conversations run with this key on the OpenAI-compatible endpoint show up as chats of the owner.

ocr.title: Document OCR
ocr.subtitle: How the text of PDFs and images is read when they are indexed into the RAG. Users choose a level for each document, up to the maximum.
ocr.serviceMissingTitle: Some OCR levels are not installed
ocr.serviceMissingDesc: The fast and structured levels need the ocr service container (the structured one only in the full image, OCR_STRUCTURED=1). Unavailable levels fall back to the nearest available one.
ocr.defaultHint: Used when the user does not choose one, and for documents indexed by agents and tools.
ocr.maxHint: Highest level users may choose. The vision level costs one AI call per page.
ocr.defaultAboveMax: The default level cannot be above the maximum level.

homeAssistant.title: Home Assistant
homeAssistant.subtitle: Home Assistant as a native integration: one connection gives the agent your home — find and control the devices exposed to Assist, their history and logbook — tells the memory who is home and in which room, and says the memory's reminders on the voice satellite of the person's room.
homeAssistant.presenceHint: Who is home (person.*) and in which room (a per-room tracker such as Bermuda on a phone or watch; a satellite that moves, such as the quacksat duck, by its place sensor); occupancy sensors count as someone in the room.
homeAssistant.busyHint: Whoever is on a call, in do-not-disturb or with a Focus on, read from the companion app's sensors on their phone, is told to the memory as busy: while they are, nothing that can wait reaches them. The sensor has to be turned on in the companion app; without it nothing is sent.
homeAssistant.voiceHint: Say the memory's initiatives on the satellite of the person's room (start a conversation when the satellite can, else an announcement); with others in the room only "I have something for you". The reply lands in the memory's chat.
homeAssistant.noRooms: nobody in a room with a voice point
homeAssistant.noWyomingUser: No Wyoming conversation user is set: presence has no memory to go to.
homeAssistant.howToDesc: At least the companion app (who is home) and one voice satellite per room; for the room, per-room Bluetooth (Bermuda with ESPHome proxies, or ESPresense) with a phone or a watch, later faces (Frigate) or a mobile satellite. In Recordare's console bind each person's homeassistant address (person.x) on their card.
homeAssistant.tokenSet: Token saved — paste a new one to replace it
homeAssistant.tokenHint: In Home Assistant: your profile → Security → Long-lived access tokens → Create token. Stored encrypted.
homeAssistant.importLabel: Or import from its MCP server
homeAssistant.importHint: Takes the URL and token of the Home Assistant MCP server and turns that server off: the native tools replace its tools.
homeAssistant.toolsHint: Find and control the devices (ha_find_entities, ha_get_state, ha_call_service), their history and logbook, calendars and to-do lists (the shopping list too), camera snapshots the agent looks at, push notifications to a phone — only on the entities exposed to Assist (Home Assistant → Settings → Voice assistants → Expose). Locks, alarms, garage doors and gates: the agent asks you first.
homeAssistant.peopleHint: Each user's person: "me", "my phone", "my room" for the tools.

integrations.subtitle: Services Arkimede integrates natively — one connection, used by the agent, the memory and the voice.
